subject: Hierarchical multi-group Poisson model: low n_eff on pooled scale priors

messages.author: 40bef15e0492270c
messages.subject: Hierarchical multi-group Poisson model: low n_eff on pooled scale priors
parts:
Hi,

I am doing an epidemiological study, where I am trying to see if some exposure (Ex) increases a subsequent event (Ev) for a given population. For every person that has the exposure, I've randomly sampled 5 controls that did not have the exposure, matched by sex and age-group. There are 10 different age groups. There are also some other covariates used for matching, but I have left them out to keep the model as simple as possible.

I want to estimate the relative risk between the Ex and Ev. To do this I have implemented a Poisson model,

Y ~ Poisson(b0 + bSex + bAge + bEx + bEv + bEx:Ev + offset)

The offset is the total number of people within a stratification group (i.e., a given combination of sex and age). To keep the number of model parameters low, I have taken the mean of an age group and used as a continous variable, instead of adding nine different variables for the age groups. The age has been scaled to mean=0 and unit variance. 

The idea is that the exponentiated interaction between the Ex and Ev is the relative risk ratio (~relative risk). To complete the model, I've specified that the coefficients of the linear model has normal priors, and the scale of the normal distribution is determined by a truncated t-distribution with 7 df. I have put a pretty constrained prior on the scale for the sex and age coefficients, since I expect these to be very, very close to zero due to the case-control structure. Some experiments with scale=1 on the coefficients indicate that the magnitude of the sex and age coefficients is between 10^-4 to 10^-6.  The coefficients for Ex, Ev and Ex:Ev are set to weakly informative, as this coefficient typically be between -1.5 and 1.5

Simulating the priors in R, I get the following (may vary due to tails of the t-distribution):

sigma <- rt(1000, df=7); sigma[sigma < 0] <- 0; beta <- rnorm(1000, 0, sigma); quantile(beta, c(2.5/100, 97.5/100))
     2.5%     97.5% 
-1.579362  1.410655 

sigma <- rt(1000, df=7); sigma[sigma < 0] <- 0; beta <- rnorm(1000, 0, sigma*0.001); quantile(beta, c(2.5/100, 97.5/100))
        2.5%        97.5% 
-0.001614221  0.001864774


Additionally, I have multiple different Ex->Ev risks I want to estimate, so I have grouped them into a hierarchical model with a pooled prior on the scale. In total I have J=52 groups. The Stan model can be seen at https://gist.github.com/demodw/df5c9b042d1de50a9694dd098385bc44. The scales for the age and sex coefficient seem to be in the order of 10^-4 to 10^-3, where the scale for the Ex, Ev and interaction is on the unit scale.

My problem is that the n_eff for the scale priors on sex and age is incredibly low and, I guess, consequently R-hat is ~1.1. with warmup=2000 and samples=2000, I get about an n_eff < 40 and n_eff/s ~ 10^-3 to 10^-4. All other parameters look acceptable. The output from stansummary can be seen at https://gist.github.com/demodw/23c31ca5304d3304f15ad2b17e35dfef. 
 The n_eff for the regression coefficients are all well above 200. Posterior predictions are actually looking OK, but I am wondering if they could be better if I found a way to increase the n_eff for the scales. 

What I have tried so far:

1. The Matt trick. I re-parameterized all parameters using the Matt-trick. No effect. The tree depth started maxing past warm-up, and the n_eff for the _raw parameters were as low as the transformed parameters. 
2. A partial Matt trick. I re-parameterized only the troublesome scale priors using the Matt trick. Same as above.
3. Changing priors. I've tried normal and gamma distributions. No effect. 
4. Varying the scale-prior. Constraining it even more gives Stan trouble exploring the posterior. 
5. Standardizing sex, even though it's a binary variable, to have mean=0 and sd=1. No effect. 
6. Switching to a negative binomial model. This actually worsens the posterior prediction, except for when Ex=0 and Ev=0. 


Any advice on how to proceed? 

Cheers, and sorry for the wall of text! I tried to describe the exact problem in detail.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Hierarchical multi-group Poisson model: low n_eff on pooled scale priors
parts:
It's often challenging to get high n_eff for the hierarchical parameters,
and often nailing them down precisely doesn't do anythnig to the posterior
predictions you care about.

You want to check consistency of your priors and posteriors---mismatches
are problematic as are any other kind of model misspecification.

Otherwise, you want to look at things like posterior pairs to see if
some of the parameter pairs produce bad geometries like bananas or
funnels. If so, that can give you a clue as to where to look.

The other thing to do is run longer warmups to make sure adaptation
have converged, then run longer chains. If the n_eff/time stays the
same and n_eff grows with iteration, you should eventually get to convergence.

- Bob
